- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. - dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). h13.

- **impl** — `*service` (unexported struct wrapping a `goldmark.Markdown`), defined in `internal/markdown/markdown.go:57-60`, satisfying the `markdown.Service` interface declared at `internal/markdown/markdown.go:31-55`. This is the only production implementation of the interface (nothing else implements `markdown.Service` outside test doubles). It internally delegates AST→markdown-text rendering to `renderer.MarkdownRenderer` (`internal/markdown/renderer/markdown_renderer.go`), a plain helper struct, not itself an interface implementation.

- **construction** — built by `markdown.NewService(...)` (`internal/markdown/markdown.go:85`). At runtime it's constructed exactly once, in `NewAPIV1Service` at `server/router/api/v1/v1.go:48-51`, with `WithTagExtension()` and `WithMentionExtension()` options. That single instance is then threaded into other components rather than re-constructed (e.g. passed as `apiV1Service.MarkdownService` into `rss.NewRSSService` in `server/server.go:85`). Other call sites of `markdown.NewService` (`server/router/rss/rss_test.go`, `server/router/fileserver/fileserver_test.go`, `server/router/api/v1/test/test_helper.go`) are test-only.

- **holders** — three structs hold the `markdown.Service` interface as a field:
  - `APIV1Service.MarkdownService` (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:35`) — the primary holder, used throughout `server/router/api/v1/*` (e.g. `memo_service.go:108,447`, `memo_service_webhooks.go:85`, `memo_mention_helpers.go:32`).
  - `RSSService.MarkdownService` (`server/router/rss/rss.go:45`) — reuses the API service's instance (see above), used at `rss.go:339` for `RenderHTML`.
  - `memopayload.Runner.MarkdownService` (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:16`) — declared and constructible via `NewRunner`, but this `Runner` type itself is never instantiated in production code (only its package-level function `RebuildMemoPayload` is called directly from `memo_service.go`, passing `s.MarkdownService`); it appears to be dead/test-only scaffolding today.
